course_description:
This course investigates the concepts and techniques of strategic analysis and implementation at the business and corporate levels. Specific concepts examined include industry and environment analysis, business strategy analysis, organisation performance analysis, capabilities analysis, gap analysis, business and corporate strategic options, strategic decision making, implementation, corporate strategic analysis, mergers and acquisitions, and strategic alliances.

The course draws upon current strategic management theory to provide a framework for evaluating the strategic positioning of firms for sustainable competitive advantage. Specifically, it explains the strategic management process - how managers develop and implement strategies in organisations - and how that process itself is changing. It focuses on three main issues: (1) how different industry conditions support different types of strategies, (2) how strategic management is shaped and deployed within the organisation, and (3) how organisations develop and maintain capabilities that lead to sustained competitive advantage. As such, the course will endeavour to provide experiential learning activities so students can appreciate how strategic management is practised in organisations.

Course Changes in Response to Previous Student Feedback

A practice week has been included for the assignment 1. This initiative will occur in week 5 and enables students to practice assimilating their knowledge from weeks 2-4 in an environment prior to a formal test. Students will be provided with formative feedback from course staff on their efforts in week 5.

course_aims: This course aims to assist you in developing an understanding of the strategic management process and provide you with an opportunity to develop your skills in developing and implementing strategic decisions.ﾠ

learning_outcomes.description: Demonstrate an in-depth knowledge about the dynamic nature of business and the role of strategy in generating and sustaining competitive advantage.
Investigate and discuss the most important internal and external influences on an organisations strategy.
Evaluate business strategies, discussing how particular courses of action may (or may not) provide competitive advantage.
Reflect critically on the issues involved in integrating the various functional activities of a firm into a coherent strategy.
Show an awareness of the fundamental uncertainties that strategic managers face in charting a firms course over time, articulating consequences and proposing solutions to resolve these challenges.
Participate collaboratively and productively as a member of a team.

assessment_details.task_description: Students will be allocated to teams and each member will be assigned to play a role on the management team of the case company. During the seminar, the management team will be asked to evaluate and make recommendations on the case company's business-level, corporate-level, collaborative strategies, and corporate governance. Students will be assessed on the quality of the strategic advice that their team provides for the case company, as well as their ability to understand and leverage organisational politics in arguing for their preferred strategy. You will have four opportunities to be assessed on your performance in the Business Simulation, and your group's best three (out of four) marks will count towards your final grade for the course (3 x 13.33 = 40%). Students who are absent for a Business Simulation meeting will receive a score of zero for that week. A student who has legitimate grounds for an absence from a Business Simulation meeting under the University's assessment policy must contact the Course Coordinator prior to, or within 24 hours of, the missed assessment and must provide appropriate supporting documentation. Your student identification card will be checked for each of the four weeks of this assessment item to verify your identity. Please ensure you bring your student ID to class. The assessment task is to completed using handwritten materials. Use of electronic devices is not permitted. Students found using electronic devices will be asked to leave the classroom and will be scored at a zero for that week's assessment. To assist with their work, groups will be provided with printed course materials related to political games, elites, and an AI-generated PESTEL, Porter, and VRIN analysis of their Wesfarmers business unit. At the conclusion of their work, groups are to inform the teaching team. One student from the group will then be permitted to take a photo of their team's output for upload into the course Blackboard site and through the relevant assessment submission link for that week. Accessing sites other than email and the course Blackboard site is not permitted. Groups should allow at least ten minutes for completion of the upload process. assessment_details.title: Reflection
assessment_details.task_description: Word Limit: 1200 words (+ or - 10%) In this individual assignment, you will reflect on your personal experience of the Business Simulation to better understand what you did well, what you could improve, and what you would do differently next time. To enable this reflection, your assignment will do the following: Describe two instances from the Business Simulation in weeks 8, 9, 10, and 11 of challenges your Business Unit or Group faced in negotiating strategic recommendations with other Business Units and Groups in the corporation. Leverage theory on strategic management and organisational politics, as covered in the course, to justify where you believe your Business Unit or Group was successful in pursuing implementation of your strategic recommendations. Leverage theory on strategic management and organisational politics, as covered in the course, to justify where you believe your Business Unit or Group was unsuccessful or could have performed better in pursuing implementation of your strategic recommendations. Leverage theory on organisational politics, as covered in the course, to explain how you would engage differently, were you to pursue negotiation around implementation of your strategic recommendations for a second time. Even if your negotiations were successful, it should be that you can identify political strategies which would have furthered your Business Unit’s strategic ambitions. Engage in effective communication of key messages around strategic management and organisational politics as covered in the course. Please note that a successful negotiation may not mean that your Business Unit or Group had its initial strategic recommendation accepted in whole. Other Business Units or Groups can improve a strategic recommendation. It is not a winner-take-all situation. A successful outcome for your Business Unit or Group should be one in which you recognise a justifiable strategy has been adopted for assisting the corporation and its subsidiaries in pursuit of their overall vision. learning_activities.topic: Course Introduction: What is strategy? In this course introduction, you will be presented with the assessment activities and an explanation of how the course will work as well as some understanding on how theorists have viewed the topic of strategic management over the years. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03, L04, L05

External Environment Analysis: PESTEL This week you will learn about PESTEL analysis. See how it was derived from the thoughts of Aguilar (1967) and learn how to apply the framework in evaluating the general external environment of the organisation. Importantly, you will be introduced to key course criteria for critiquing the quality of an AI-produced PESTEL analysis. You will also have opportunity to practice applying these criteria to an AI-generated piece of work and receive feedback from teaching staff on your efforts. This seminar is essential to your preparation for the practice test in week 5 and Assessment 1 in week 6. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L05

External Environment Analysis: Porter's Five Forces This week you will learn about Porter's Five Forces industry analysis. See how it was derived from the thoughts of Porter (1979) and learn how to apply the framework in evaluating the external industry environment of the organisation. Importantly, you will be introduced to key course criteria for critiquing the quality of an AI-produced Porter's Five Forces analysis. You will also have opportunity to practice applying these criteria to an AI-generated piece of work and receive feedback from teaching staff on your efforts. This seminar is essential to your preparation for the practice test in week 5 and Assessment 1 in week 6. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L05

Internal Environment Analysis: VRIN This week you will learn about VRIN analysis. See how it was derived from the thoughts of Barney (1991) and learn how to apply the framework in evaluating the internal environment of the organisation. Importantly, you will be introduced to key course criteria for critiquing the quality of an AI-produced VRIN analysis. You will also have opportunity to practice applying these criteria to an AI-generated piece of work and receive feedback from teaching staff on your efforts. This seminar is essential to your preparation for the practice test in week 5 and Assessment 1 in week 6. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L05

In-class Practice in Readiness for Assessment 1 This week's seminar will be essential preparation for Assessment 1. You will be placed into groups with other students. You will then be presented with an AI generated PESTEL, Porter, and VRIN analysis of a case study organisation. Your role in your groups is to apply the criteria associated with PESTEL, Porter, and VRIN analysis as outlined in weeks 2-4 and to assess the quality of the AI generated output you have been provided. You will receive feedback from the teaching team on the quality of your work. The intention is that you will use this week's work to practice applying the criteria for assessing the AI produced output, thereby becoming better prepared for Assessment 1 in week 6. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L06

Assessment 1: Individual In-class Case Study Analysis This assessment is to be completed as an individual task. This week you will engage in your in-class assessment. You will be provided with an AI generated PESTEL, Porter's Five Forces, and VRIN analysis of a case study organisation. Your task will be to apply your understanding of key criteria introduced in weeks 2, 3, and 4 to assess the quality of the AI generated output. You must submit your assessment prior to leaving class. Please note that no electronic materials will be permitted for use in this test. However, you may bring along one A4 sheet (double sided and written only in English language) compiled with handwritten notes to assist you. Further information on the test can be found on the course BlackBoard site. Learning outcomes: L01, L02

The Politics of Strategy This week will introduce you to the idea of strategy as politics. How do successful strategists navigate political games and elites in order to implement strategy? The session will also serve as a practice for Assessment 2 in the coming weeks. You will come together in your teams and practice your decision making and negotiation skills. Please note this seminar is essential preparation for Assessment 2. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03, L04, L05

Business-Level Strategy This week will be the first of the in-class assessments as part of Assessment 2 - Business Simulation. You will explore the topic of business-level strategy by making decisions and negotiating on behalf of your Wesfarmers Strategic Business Unit. Please note no electronic materials are permitted for completing this exercise. More information on the assessment item can be found on the course BlackBoard site. Learning outcomes: L02, L03, L04, L05, L06

Corporate-Level Strategy This week will be the second of the in-class assessments as part of Assessment 2 - Business Simulation.
